speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned a chronic cough and recurrent bronchitis; to help me understand your condition, how long has this cough been persisting, and do you notice any specific triggers or accompanying symptoms like wheezing, fever, or shortness of breath?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old woman. The patient has been experiencing an aggressive cough producing copious amounts of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum for about 11 years, with exacerbations similar to the current presentation today. Reports that the cough is worse in the morning and has had multiple evaluations in the past due to recurrent bouts of bronchitis requiring antibiotics treatment. The patient is a non-smoker.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Bronchiectasis.

The 11-year history of an aggressive cough with copious, thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum, particularly in the mornings, combined with recurrent bronchitis exacerbations requiring antibiotics in a non-smoker, is highly characteristic of bronchiectasis. To confirm this diagnosis and assess the extent of airway damage, please request the following imaging and tests: REQUEST TEST: Sputum_Culture; REQUEST TEST: CT_Chest_High_Resolution; REQUEST IMAGES.
